Alright, let me think this through. I've been working these 8 mu for most of my life, same wheat-maize rotation my father did, though we do things smarter now than back then. With just me and the missus at home, and the kids working in town, labor is my real headache — not the knowledge, not even the money so much. So a lot of my plan is built around hiring the combine and the no-till seeder at the right moment, because I can't do it all by hand anymore at 65.

**Wheat (winter, all 8 mu):**

I'll plant around October 10–15, after the maize comes off. I usually go with Jimai 22 or whatever good seed the agro-supply shop has — I don't save my own anymore, the certified seed germinates better and I can taste the difference in yield. About 12–13 kg of seed per mu, drilled in rows.

For fertilizer, my routine is a compound 15-15-15 at sowing, around 40 kg/mu as base — that gives me roughly 6 kg N, 6 kg P₂O₅, 6 kg K₂O up front. Then at jointing in early spring, I topdress 20–22 kg of urea, which is about another 9–10 kg N. So I'm putting on around 15–16 kg N total per mu. I know the extension station pushes 18, but on my soil with the maize stalks returned every summer, 16 is enough — pushing higher doesn't pay back at current grain prices.

Irrigation: wheat here can't survive without it. I'll water at sowing if the soil is dry, then the overwintering water around early December, then jointing in late March, then grain-fill in early May. Four irrigations is my standard. The well meter costs me about 35 yuan per mu per round, so this is the biggest cash item after fertilizer.

Weeds — I'll spray a herbicide once in late winter for the broadleaves and ryegrass. Aphids I watch for around heading; some years I spray, some years not.

I expect around 480 kg/mu if the spring isn't too dry. Last year I got 470, the year before 500.

**Maize (summer, same 8 mu):**

Right after wheat harvest in mid-June, I hire the no-till seeder to drill maize straight into the wheat stubble. There's no time for tillage — three or four days at most. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or one of the newer ones, about 2.5 kg/mu.

Fertilizer for maize I keep simpler. I broadcast about 50 kg/mu of a 28-6-8 compound at the V6 stage when I cultivate between rows — that's about 14 kg N, 3 kg P, 4 kg K. Sometimes I add another 5 kg of urea at tasseling if the leaves look pale, but most years I don't bother. Maize here gets a lot from the wheat residue and the summer rains.

Irrigation for maize — usually I only need to water once at sowing to get a stand, and maybe once at tasseling if July is dry. The summer monsoon does most of the work.

Pests: corn borer is the main worry. I'll spray once with an insecticide around tasseling. Weeds I get with a pre-emergence herbicide right after planting.

Maize yield I'm targeting 530 kg/mu — that's what I've averaged the last few years.

**On costs and labor:** total cash inputs across both crops will run me around 6,500 yuan for the year. The two of us can handle most of the field work — spraying, irrigation, walking the fields — but I pay for the combine on wheat (about 60 yuan/mu), the no-till maize seeder (50 yuan/mu), and the maize harvester (80 yuan/mu). At my age that money is well spent.
